key_insight: Drive My Way (DMW) aligns a vision-language-action model to individual driving preferences, enabling a single end-to-end system to interpret natural-language intent and produce personalized driving behaviors instead of one-size-fits-all actions.
problem_solved: Existing end-to-end driving systems optimize for generic objectives or use fixed driving modes, failing to adapt to long-term habits and short-term intentions of individual drivers or to interpret natural-language preferences.
method: Extend a vision-language-action (VLA) model with a preference-conditioned policy: fuse visual inputs, language intent, and a learned driver-preference embedding to produce control actions.

Train/align the model using preference signals (e.g., demonstrations, labeled comparisons, or language annotations) so behaviors reflect individual acceleration, braking, merging and overtaking styles.
Evaluate personalization and intent-following in simulation and/or real-world scenarios, comparing personalized policies to generic baselines on safety, comfort, and preference satisfaction metrics.
impact: Enables human-centered autonomous driving that adapts to individual styles and accepts natural-language instructions, improving user acceptance and personalization in deployed driving AI systems. Practitioners can reuse the preference-alignment pattern for other embodied V-L-A tasks.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: VLA pipeline showing camera input + language intent + preference embedding → controller outputs (steering, throttle, brake).
Before/after trajectory comparison: generic policy vs. preference-conditioned policy across the same scenario (e.g., merging/overtaking) with metrics (comfort, similarity to driver).
Interface mockup: user issuing a natural-language driving preference (e.g., “be cautious and maintain larger gaps”) and corresponding policy adjustment.
Evaluation heatmap or bar chart: trade-offs among safety, comfort, and preference-satisfaction across multiple driver profiles.
paper_title: Drive My Way: Preference Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model for Personalized Driving
paper_authors: Zehao Wang, Huaide Jiang, Shuaiwu Dong, Yuping Wang, Hang Qiu
